— How I work

Clear priorities.
Practical progress.

An engagement should make the work easier to understand: what we are solving, what is included, who is responsible, and how the result will be checked.

From understanding to action

01

Understand

Your business, customers, and the outcome you need.

02

Review

The website, marketing, and systems already in place.

03

Prioritize

A focused plan with clear scope and responsibilities.

04

Build & refine

Implement agreed work, review signals, and decide what comes next.

Start with the business, not the tool

We begin with your offering, customers, goals, and constraints. Useful background includes the current website, existing marketing activity, available reporting, and what has already been tried. You do not need a technical brief to explain a business problem.

Review the current setup

A review establishes what is working, what is uncertain, and which dependencies need attention. This might involve the website, search visibility, advertising accounts, measurement, or connected systems. Access is requested only for the agreed work and should be arranged securely.

Agree a focused scope

The plan defines deliverables, responsibilities, assumptions, timing, and third-party requirements. An SEO audit is different from implementation; a website build is different from ongoing maintenance. Those boundaries should be clear before work starts.

Implement and verify

Agreed changes are checked against the intended behavior. A form must really deliver before it is called functional; tracking must distinguish a completed action from a click; content must reflect accurate business facts. Work involving another provider needs a clear handoff and owner.

Review what happens next

Where monitoring or ongoing work is included, we review meaningful signals and decide what to improve. Not every project includes every stage or an ongoing management arrangement. Additional work is discussed when it addresses a real need rather than assumed as part of the original scope.
